items.author: Soein
items.body:
## Summary

Add deduplication and consolidation capabilities for Archival Memory passages to reduce redundancy and improve retrieval efficiency for long-running agents.

## Motivation

Currently, Letta has excellent tools for Core Memory management:
- `rethink_memory()` / `memory_rethink()` - completely rewrite memory blocks
- `memory_replace()` / `memory_insert()` - precise edits

However, **Archival Memory (passages) lacks similar consolidation mechanisms**. Over time, this leads to:

1. **Redundant passages**: Similar information stored multiple times
2. **Semantic duplicates**: Same facts
items.title: Feature Request: Archival Memory Deduplication and Consolidation

items.author: kaaloo
items.body:
## Problem Statement

Users cannot migrate conversations between agents or projects. When moving an agent to a new project (e.g., from development to production), all conversation history is lost.

## Current State

The Letta API supports:
- Exporting agents via `.af` files (includes config, memory blocks, tools)
- Listing conversations: `GET /v1/conversations?agent_id=xxx`
- Listing messages: `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages`
- Creating conversations: `POST /v1/conversations` (creates empty conversation only)

**What's missing:**
- No way to create a conversation with pre-existing message
items.title: Feature Request: Conversation Import API for Agent Migration

items.author: ezra-letta
items.body:
## Summary

Agent-level `compaction_settings` with `mode: sliding_window` and `sliding_window_percentage: 0.15` (evict 15%, keep 85%) performs a full context wipe instead of partial eviction. After compaction, only the summary message remains -- all conversation history is gone.

## Environment

- Letta server 0.16.6 (self-hosted Docker on ECS)
- Model: Qwen 3.5 27b via LM Studio (llama.cpp backend, Vulkan)
- Context window: 45,000 tokens
- Agent-level compaction settings applied via PATCH:
  ```json
  {"compaction_settings": {"mode": "sliding_window", "sliding_window_percentage": 0.15}}
  ```
items.title: sliding_window compaction ignores percentage, performs full context wipe

items.author: ayushin
items.body:
## Problem

PR #10009 (`a882310e`) introduced SSRF protection in `letta/helpers/url_validation.py` that blocks MCP server URLs resolving to non-public IPs. This breaks **all** Docker-based development setups where the MCP server runs on the host machine.

**Error:**
```
Error executing tool get_file_text: Hostname resolves to non-public IP: 192.168.65.254
```

This happens because `host.docker.internal` (the standard Docker mechanism for containers to reach host services) resolves to `192.168.65.254` (Docker Desktop bridge IP). The SSRF check in `validate_mcp_server_url()` rejects this as a no
items.title: MCP SSRF protection needs allow-list for Docker/local development
